body.text:
**Squash-merge is fixed** — committed and pushed (`5e23b54`), with the docs updated as part of the finish-up per your new standing rule.

The fix in brief: since `SQUASH_MSG` exists at commit-msg time but is deleted before post-commit (both facts verified empirically before writing a line), the fold runs in two phases. At commit-msg, the hook detects the squash, reads the squashed commit SHAs out of `SQUASH_MSG`, and injects the *surviving* change's id — the oldest squashed commit's change, matching the fold rule rebase-squash already uses — as the trailer, leaving a pending-fold handoff file in the git dir. At post-commit, that file is consumed (always deleted once seen) and the remaining squashed changes are absorbed through the exact same §7.4 machinery as a rebase squash. The stale-file guard is airtight: the fold only fires if the committed trailer matches the recorded survivor id, which a commit aborted between the two hooks can never satisfy. And a nice subtlety that fell out for free — the squashed commits' own trailers quoted inside `SQUASH_MSG` can't confuse anything, because git indents quoted messages and the trailer regex only matches at line start.

`doctor` also gained the companion audit: any change whose head no branch or tag can reach (i.e., pre-fix squash-then-delete history) now warns with a `relink`-or-tag remediation, with our metadata refs deliberately excluded from what counts as "reachable."

Proof: 7 new tests (212 CLI total, all green), and the *exact* live scenario that exposed the bug yesterday — squash-merge a two-commit branch, delete the branch — now produces one continued change with the second absorbed, and a doctor that reports **no anomalies**.

That's step 1 of the desktop build order done. Step 2 is the read-only API groundwork (`rev` param on overview, `/api/branches`, `/api/diff/:sha`) — which makes the branch sidebar and diff-with-intent pane land in the plain browser before Electron even enters the picture. Say the word.

The warnings come from `core.autocrlf=true` in your global config: the repo stores LF (correct), your working tree files are being written as LF by the tools, and git warns that it *would* convert them to CRLF next time it touches them. Two-part fix — your global setting, plus making the repo authoritative so it never depends on anyone's global config again.

**Your global config (run once, anywhere):**

```
git config --global core.autocrlf false
```

That stops the conversion behavior entirely — modern Windows tooling (VS Code, Node, git itself) is perfectly happy with LF files, and `false` is the cleanest setting when repos declare their own line endings. (The conservative alternative is `input` — converts CRLF→LF on commit but never rewrites your working tree — either kills the warnings.)

**The repo side I'll do now** — a `.gitattributes` that pins LF for every text file regardless of any machine's config:

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git add .gitattributes && git add --renormalize . && git status --short | head -10 && echo "--- renormalize diff count: $(git diff --cached --numstat | wc -l) files staged ---"

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add .gitattributes: LF everywhere, decided by the repo

Kills the CRLF warning noise on Windows and removes line endings from
the machine-config lottery. Extra weight here: blob SHAs key the
embedding cache and scope items, so a CRLF-flipped file would silently
re-embed as new content. git add --renormalize found one CRLF file
(CLAUDE.md, from a hand edit) - normalized, content unchanged.

Owner-side companion (documented, run per machine):
  git config --global core.autocrlf false

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin main "+refs/notes/git-for-ai/*:refs/notes/git-for-ai/*" "+refs/git-for-ai/*:refs/git-for-ai/*" 2>&1 | tail -3

summary: claude-code session: 3 tool execution(s), 2 model turn(s) for commit "Add .gitattributes: LF everywhere, decided by the repo".
